interim_updates.note_text: CIC Holdings Group's Q1 FY2026/27 revenue grew 2.7% YoY to Rs.22,029.41Mn while gross profit rose faster at 10.3% to Rs.6,008.05Mn, and Operating Profit grew 12.7% to Rs.3,199.61Mn -- but the segmental mix behind that growth is uneven. Livestock Solutions segment PBT more than doubled, from Rs.312.37Mn to Rs.660.25Mn (+111.4%), on segment revenue growth of 10.1% to Rs.4,895.84Mn, and Industrial Solutions PBT rose 62.2% (Rs.329.12Mn to Rs.533.90Mn) as segment revenue jumped 40.7% to Rs.2,628.18Mn. These gains were partly offset by Agri Solutions -- the Group's largest segment -- where PBT fell 16.6% from Rs.1,294.81Mn to Rs.1,080.56Mn as segment revenue declined 7.5% to Rs.9,974.42Mn. Health & Personal Care was roughly flat (PBT -4.0% to Rs.662.51Mn on revenue +1.4%). Below operating profit, net finance cost rose 16.4% to Rs.613.00Mn (finance cost +16.1% to Rs.676.67Mn vs finance income +14.0% to Rs.63.67Mn), but PBT growth (+17.5%) outpaced Operating Profit growth because of Rs.170.65Mn in net non-operating/equity-accounted items: a Rs.103.56Mn gain on bargain purchase, Rs.82.64Mn share of profit from equity-accounted investees (mainly John Keells Holdings PLC, JKH), partly offset by a Rs.15.55Mn loss on dilution of the JKH stake (JKH exercised employee share options, diluting CIC's holding). Tax expense rose 13.7% to Rs.951.96Mn. PAT (Group) grew 19.7% to Rs.1,809.35Mn, of which Rs.1,507.75Mn (+23.2%) was attributable to equity holders and Rs.301.60Mn to non-controlling interests.

YoY figures use GROUP (consolidated) basis and the filing's own 30 June 2025 comparative column, per standard convention (a COMPANY/standalone basis row was also stored in financial_statements but is not used for this narrative).
interim_updates.takeaway: Group PBT growth of 17.5% overstates underlying operating momentum: Rs.170.65Mn of the increase came from non-recurring/equity-accounted items tied to the John Keells Holdings stake (a Rs.103.56Mn bargain-purchase gain and Rs.82.64Mn share of associate profit, less a Rs.15.55Mn dilution loss), not the core CIC business. Core Operating Profit still grew a solid 12.7% to Rs.3,199.61Mn, but that was driven almost entirely by Livestock Solutions (+111.4% segment PBT) and Industrial Solutions (+62.2%), while Agri Solutions -- the largest segment -- saw PBT decline 16.6% to Rs.1,080.56Mn.
operational_highlights: Group revenue grew 2.7% YoY to Rs.22,029.41Mn while gross profit rose faster at 10.3% to Rs.6,008.05Mn.
Livestock Solutions segment PBT more than doubled, from Rs.312.37Mn to Rs.660.25Mn (+111.4%), on 10.1% segment revenue growth.
Industrial Solutions segment PBT rose 62.2% (Rs.329.12Mn to Rs.533.90Mn) as segment revenue jumped 40.7% to Rs.2,628.18Mn.
Agri Solutions, the largest segment, saw PBT fall 16.6% (Rs.1,294.81Mn to Rs.1,080.56Mn) as segment revenue declined 7.5% to Rs.9,974.42Mn.
Net finance cost rose 16.4% to Rs.613.00Mn as finance cost grew 16.1% to Rs.676.67Mn, outpacing finance income growth of 14.0%.

Non-operating items added a net Rs.170.65Mn to PBT: a Rs.103.56Mn gain on bargain purchase and Rs.82.64Mn share of profit from equity-accounted investee JKH, partly offset by a Rs.15.55Mn dilution loss on the same JKH stake.
key_drivers: Livestock Solutions (+111.4% segment PBT) and Industrial Solutions (+62.2%) are the specific drivers of Group profit growth this quarter, not Agri Solutions.
Agri Solutions' 16.6% PBT decline (Rs.1,294.81Mn -> Rs.1,080.56Mn) on a 7.5% revenue drop is a specific drag worth monitoring given it remains the largest segment.

The John Keells Holdings PLC equity-accounted stake (net +Rs.170.65Mn to PBT via bargain-purchase gain, associate profit share, and dilution loss) is a specific non-operating swing factor behind the 17.5% PBT growth headline.
